scope: Model/editor semantic and pedagogy review of Lesson 0130; not an independent human or real-learner test.

englishNaturalness.evidence: ‘My mind is full of questions.’ and ‘My mind is clear now.’ are grammatical, natural controlled uses of mind in the intended thoughts/thinking sense.

persianMeaningQuality.evidence: Persian copy maps mind to «ذهن» consistently and preserves the mental-state meaning.

pedagogicalClarity.evidence: The target is recognized, practiced, heard in context, transferred to a second mental state, and retrieved without answer exposure.

distractorQuality.evidence: Distractors keep familiar syntax but substitute semantically incompatible nouns.

dialoguePlausibility.evidence: لیام و لیو در کتابخانه بعد از مرور برنامه امتحان درباره تمرکز و سؤال‌هایشان حرف می‌زنند.

difficultyFit.evidence: The lexical idea is abstract but production remains two short controlled A1-compatible sentences.

repetitionUsefulness.evidence: mind recurs across recognition, dialogue, comprehension, transfer, and hidden retrieval.

transferQuality.evidence: The learner moves from ‘full of questions’ to ‘clear now’ while retaining the same noun sense.

overallCoherence.evidence: Outcome, story, target construction, learner turns, and assessment remain aligned.

learnerExperience.evidence: No real learner test is claimed; perceived difficulty of the abstract concept remains unverified.

limitations: No independent human or real learner test has been performed.
Only the bounded thoughts/thinking noun sense of mind is reviewed.
Generated audio pronunciation/prosody is not evaluated at this text stage.
